🧹 Nitpick comments (1)
test/e2e/cluster_samples_operator_test.go (1)
`107-114`: **Close the pod log stream after `io.ReadAll`.** `req.Stream` returns a `ReadCloser`; not closing it inside this loop can leak resources during long test runs.
Proposed fix ```diff readCloser, err := req.Stream(context.TODO()) if err != nil { t.Fatalf("error getting pod logs for container %s: %s", container.Name, err.Error()) } b, err := io.ReadAll(readCloser) + closeErr := readCloser.Close() if err != nil { t.Fatalf("error reading pod stream %s", err.Error()) } + if closeErr != nil { + t.Logf("error closing pod log stream for container %s: %s", container.Name, closeErr.Error()) + } podLog := string(b) ```
🤖 Prompt for AI Agents ``` Verify each finding against the current code and only fix it if needed. In `@test/e2e/cluster_samples_operator_test.go` around lines 107 - 114, The pod log stream returned by req.Stream is not being closed, which can leak resources; after successfully obtaining readCloser (from req.Stream) ensure it is closed regardless of io.ReadAll outcome—for example, wrap the streaming+read logic in a small anonymous func or call readCloser.Close() in a defer immediately after the nil check so that readCloser.Close() always runs even if io.ReadAll (or subsequent logic) returns an error; update the block that uses readCloser, req.Stream, io.ReadAll and container.Name to guarantee the stream is closed. ```
